_doc: Revert-verify mutants for issue #4379 — a top-level block scalar read as its RAW text, and the consumers of that read. Mutants are type-preserving (an impossible-but-valid condition / `x || f(x)` keeping the import used), never `if (false)` (integration-test-revert-verify §A36). `red_re` anchors on the `● <suite> › [Xn]` header (§A44/§A104). Subject: yamlScalar.ts.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/utilities/yamlScalar.ts

M5_folded_not_a_header._note: `>` (63 of 106 live headers) is not recognised as a block scalar.

M6_decode_standalone._note: The raw text is read as a standalone document instead of a top-level value — an explicit indentation indicator is re-based on column -1. It also reddens D5: standalone, js-yaml ACCEPTS a tab-indented body (`|\n\tx` → `\tx\n`) that it rejects as a key's value — the wrapper is what makes the rejected body come back verbatim.
M6_decode_standalone.from: const loaded = yaml.load(`k: ${raw}`) as { k?: unknown } | null;
M6_decode_standalone.to: const loaded = { k: yaml.load(raw) } as { k?: unknown } | null;

M7_quoted_decoder_skips_blocks._note: `decodeYamlQuotedScalar` (the `$target.<prop>` decoder) no longer delegates block scalars.

M8_item_not_reindented._note: The body is written as a list item verbatim — js-yaml rejects the whole frontmatter (`bad indentation`).

M13_item_indicator_decoded._note: A list item's explicit indentation indicator is decoded in top-level context — re-based, so a different value falsely dedups (PR #4400 review LOW-1).

M14_rejected_body_emptied._note: A body js-yaml rejects is emptied instead of returned verbatim (PR #4400 review LOW-4).
